correctness.rationale: Exhaustiveness follows from the unique bipartition of any connected graph, complete nonzero incidence-mask multiset generation, column coverage, connectivity, and canonical side-preserving row/column actions. Every candidate not discharged by open-twin automorphisms is retained and checked by independent exact full graph automorphism enumeration, including balanced side-swaps. The tested totals are 224 nine-vertex candidates and 1810 ten-vertex candidates; independent Python enumerates all 49,333 connected row-mask representations at order nine with zero failures. Exactly two nonisomorphic ten-vertex failures are recovered. Complete unlabeled counts independently match OEIS 730/4032. Witness adjacency masks, stable classes and orbits are explicitly certified. Computations establish a finite statement only.

value.rationale: The exact minimal-order obstruction and the complete first-exception classification for all connected bipartite graphs are natural invariants of the refinement-versus-automorphism question. Two independent mechanisms occur at the same sharp cutoff: a (3,2)-biregular subdivision with an unseen edge-multiplicity distinction, and a cubic ten-vertex graph with hidden nontransitive orbit structure. This is not determined by the old graph-count sequence or by between-graph counting equivalence, and is reusable as a boundary benchmark for individualization and fractional symmetry.
